questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Lithuania?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Overview” part of the Lithuania article.

questions.proof: Vilnius is the capital and largest city.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Lithuania?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Lithuania on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Lithuania article.

questions.proof: It borders Latvia to the north, Belarus to the southeast, Poland to the south and Russia to the southwest.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Lithuania?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Overview” part of the Lithuania article.

questions.proof: The national language is the Lithuanian language, which is spoken by around 3 million people.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The first radio station was started in _____ in Kaunas.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Radio and television” part of the Lithuania article.

questions.proof: The first radio station was started in 1926 in Kaunas.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The first television station started in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Radio and television” part of the Lithuania article.

questions.proof: The first television station started in 1957.
